title: Strain-controlled topology and quantum control at a cubic Ce$^{3+}$ crystal-field crossing
abstract: Field-tuned crystal-field crossings provide a route to synthetic topology in localized rare-earth degrees of freedom when symmetry-resolved perturbations can independently control the crossing states. Here we show that a field-induced crossing in cubic Ce$^{3+}$ has precisely this structure. For $B\parallel[001]$, the crossing is protected by a twofold rotation, while the $T_{2g}$ shears $ε_{xz}$ and $ε_{yz}$ break that protection and mix the two states through orthogonal pseudospin components. Together with magnetic-field detuning, these controls generate an isolated diabolical point with unit-magnitude Chern charge in a three-dimensional parameter space. Using the CeTe crystal-field scale gives an ideal single-ion crossing near $35.5$ T. A calibrated point-charge calculation gives a representative projected shear coupling $|α_{T_{2g}}|\simeq18.1$ meV per unit tensor strain, corresponding to gaps of $0.036$ and $0.072$ meV for tensor shears of $0.10\%$ and $0.20\%$. We identify the associated elastic and magnetic signatures, discuss the limitations of the electrostatic estimate in a hybridizing Ce compound, and determine the adiabatic and coherence requirements for cyclic geometric control. The result is a symmetry-based framework that connects high-field crystal-field reconstruction, strain response, and parameter-space topology in rare-earth systems.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework showing how strain and magnetic fields can control the topology of electronic states at a crystal-field crossing in Ce3+. By analyzing the effective Hamiltonian, the authors predict the existence of a topologically non-trivial point (Chern charge = 1) that can be accessed by tuning strain and magnetic field, offering a route for quantum control in rare-earth materials.
main_problem: To establish a symmetry-based framework connecting high-field crystal-field reconstruction, strain response, and parameter-space topology in rare-earth systems.
main_result: The combination of strain and field detuning can generate an isolated diabolical point with unit-magnitude Chern charge in the 3D control space of a cubic Ce3+ ion.
method: Theoretical derivation using an effective two-level Hamiltonian, analyzing the topological features (Chern charge) generated by independent strain and magnetic field controls.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using the cubic Ce3+ ion ($4f^1$) crystal-field splitting, governed by an effective Hamiltonian that incorporates strain ($\epsilon_{xz}, \epsilon_{yz}$) and magnetic field detuning ($\delta B$).
key_observables: Chern charge ($|C|=1$), gap opening ($\propto |\epsilon_{\perp}|$), elastic susceptibility ($\delta c_{44}$), and geometric phase ($\gamma_{\pm}$).
important_parameters: Ideal crossing field near $35.5 	ext{ T}$ (for CeTe); representative shear coupling $|\alpha_{T2g}| \simeq 18.1 	ext{ meV}$ per unit tensor strain.
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a single-ion point-charge model, which neglects full hybridization effects in the actual compound.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectrum at the CeTe scale, the gap opening due to strain, and the Bloch-sphere trajectory used to calculate the Berry phase for quantum control.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the symmetry-protected crossing, deriving the effective Hamiltonian, calculating the topological invariant (Chern charge) using strain and field detuning as controls, and finally discussing the experimental signatures (elastic/magnetic).
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, symmetry-dictated pathway to engineer topological quantum states (diabolical points) using external, controllable parameters like mechanical strain, which is highly relevant for quantum control in solid-state systems.

(b) Exact six-level spectrum for B ∥[001], measured from the zero-field Γ7 energy. The two lowest branches belong to different C2z sectors and cross at Bc ≃35.5 T.

FIG. 2. Projected avoided crossing for ϵyz = 0 and tensor shears ϵxz = 0, 0.10%, and 0.20%, using the CeTe bench- mark |αT2g| = 18.1 meV per unit tensor strain obtained from the calibrated point-charge calculation described in Sec. III B. The corresponding minimum gaps are 0, 0.0362, and 0.0724 meV.

FIG. 3. Ideal cubic single-ion crossing field as a function of the zero-field CEF splitting, with Bc ≃12.87 ∆cub T when ∆cub is expressed in meV. The markers use representative re- ported CEF splittings for CeBi, CeInAg2, CeTe, and CeSb [22, 26, 27]. Horizontal lines indicate representative 45 T dc and 100 T pulsed-field capabilities demonstrated experimen- tally [28, 29]. The plotted values are screening estimates, not complete high-field phase-diagram predictions.

FIG. 4. Ideal two-level responses for T = 0.5, 1, 2, and 4 K. (a) Normalized magnitude of the T2g elastic softening around the crossing. (b) Crossing contribution to the differential magnetization. Its integral through the reconstructed crossing is 0.78137 µB per Ce in the linear two-level model. The plotted curves show the equilibrium local response; quantitative ultrasound in field can contain additional rotational and dynamical magnetoelastic contributions.

FIG. 5. Geometric phase from circular shear control. (a) Bloch-sphere trajectory of the lower eigenstate for a circular T2g shear drive. The displayed example uses |αT2g| = 18.1 meV per unit tensor strain, ϵ0 = 0.20%, and |Bz −Bc| = 1.5 T. (b) Lower-state Berry phase for counterclockwise (CCW) and clockwise (CW) loops on the Bz ≤Bc side. Circulation is defined as viewed from positive dz, and phases are defined modulo 2π.
